messages:
Maya: noticing elevated pod evictions in az1 this morning, GPU nodes flapping, autoscaler not creating replacements :thinking_face:
Liam: saw same from our alerting, node status goes NotReady then kubelet fails to register
infra-bot: ALERT az1 internal-dns: packet loss > 6% to metadata/registry endpoints (detected by netprobe)
Maya: that explains image pull + kubelet cert fetch failures. Any idea if this is a global control-plane blip or per-az networking?
Serena: cloud provider reported degraded fabric for az1 starting ~06:20 UTC, they flagged DNS resolver issues in subnet fabric
Karim: autoscaler error logs show "failed to bootstrap node: could not resolve metadata.google.internal" — so provisioning runs but init fails
Liam: autoscaler keeps spinning up VMs then they fail provisioning and get deleted, wasteful. Cost alarm already tripped :grimacing:
Maya: we need a fast mitigation: prevent autoscaler from repeating failed attempts and shift traffic away from az1 GPUs
Karim: suggested steps: 1) scale down low-priority batch jobs 2) taint az1 app nodes to stop new workloads 3) enable fallback routing to eu-central2 for production traffic
Maya: doing 2 & 3 now. Commands: ```kubectl taint nodes -l region=az1 dedicated=isolated:NoSchedule``` and flip router policy in the console to prefer eu-central2 for model-serving routes
ops-oncall: already reduced batch replicas by 60% (jobs queue paused), freeing ~10 GPUs
Serena: opened ticket with provider, they say "investigating DNS resolvers" and acknowledged impact to instance bootstrap. ETA unknown
Liam: we should also avoid autoscaler continuing to consume quota in az1. I'll patch the autoscaler config to set max-unready-percentage=20 and scale-down-delay=15m for az1 pool
Maya: patch applied to autoscaler configmap, roll out in progress :white_check_mark:
Karim: note: some private deployments (customer VPCs) are failing KMS unwrap calls during model load — logs show increased KMS timeouts when routed via az1 KMS proxy
Serena: that's troubling — if KMS timeouts persist we need to failover KMS traffic to backup HSM region. Do we have a fallback KMS endpoint?
Maya: yes, for enterprise customers we have configured regional KMS mirrors in eu-central2 and us-west2, but switching requires rekeying and a rolling restart of private control-plane components
Liam: short-term workaround for web-serving (non-sensitive) models: enable "local-signing-mode" for cached shard loads so we can serve from cache while KMS issue persists (measurements show no customer-sensitive keys required). Need approval from security though
Karim: security ok with local-signing for staged models for up to 3 hours under incident SOP. I'll enable it for model cache loaders: ```REDWOOD_LOCAL_SIGNING=true ./cache-warmup --models production_list```
ops-oncall: routing change to prefer eu-central2 completed, traffic shifted ~75% over last 10m, p95 latency increased ~80ms but within SLA for most customers
Maya: good. We should also pre-warm eu-central nodes to reduce cold-starts. Liam can you kick off an on-demand node group?
Liam: kicked off nodegroup prewarm: +24 GPU nodes in eu-central2 (on-demand). ETA nodes ready ~8m
Serena: note on cost: running extra on-demand nodes will increase run-rate ~23% if this persists a day. Flagging finance + growth to expect potential uplift
Karim: to reduce churn we should block autoscaler in az1 from creating new instances until provider resolves. I've added an annotation `infra.redwood/allow-provisioning=false` to az1 nodepool in the cloud-manager
Maya: nice. Also adding a temporary routing policy in smart-router to penalize az1 by 1000 weight so failovers stay stable
ops-oncall: provider update: their DNS resolver cluster is degraded, they recommend "use alternate resolver X" — but changing resolver requires node restart and cloud-init churn
Liam: we don't want more churn. Better to keep az1 nodes cordoned, let eu-central carry load. If customer private control planes are pinned to az1 we need outreach (CS)
Maya: pinging CS and Customer Pager for customers with VPC deployments in az1. Example message: "We're routing model traffic away from az1 and enabling fallbacks while provider resolves DNS. Some private deployments may see delayed model loads — working on KMS mirror failover."
Serena: Provider support says fix is targeted in next maintenance window in ~3h. If that slips we should escalate to an engineer-level contact
Karim: plan summary I pushed to incident doc: 1) cordon az1 nodes 2) block autoscaler in az1 3) prewarm eu-central2 nodes 4) enable local-signing for cached non-sensitive models 5) initiate KMS mirror failover for enterprise private control-planes (manual) 6) monitor cost burn and rollback when stable
Maya: executing KMS mirror failover for two affected private tenants now (staged, one at a time). Will post logs when done
ops-oncall: KMS failover step 1 completed for tenant-42, control-plane reported successful rewrap, model loads resumed for tenant-42 :tada:
Liam: eu-central prewarm nodes healthy, router now reporting steady state, p99 tokenization latency unchanged, generation p95 up ~120ms overall
Serena: closing on comms — draft status update for customers: short blurb about provider DNS impact, mitigation steps (traffic shifted, prewarmed capacity, some private deployments failing over KMS), ask to expect transient latency. I'll post in status.redwood and notify enterprise SLs
Maya: any remaining actions?
Karim: keep autoscaler blocked in az1 until provider confirms resolver healthy, monitor KMS error rate <1% for 30m post-failover, then slowly re-enable az1 with small canary traffic
Maya: agreed. Thanks team — great rapid coordination. I'll keep this thread updated with provider ETA and any cost estimates from finance
ops-oncall: incident channel will remain open. If provider writes "fix deployed" we run: ```for pool in az1; do kubectl uncordon -l region=$pool; terraform apply -var=allow_provisioning=true; done```
Maya: marking incident as mitigated for now, but not resolved until provider confirms and KMS stable 30m after uncordon. :lock:
